# ALS evidence packet — draft v1

This curated input is not a comprehensive review. Every method receives the same UTF-8 file. Summaries are original paraphrases. Bibliographic metadata and abstracts were checked through the public NCBI ID converter and PubMed EFetch on 2026-10-05. Selected studies predate 2025; this does not remove knowledge already in a model's training. Co-Scientist outputs are not included.

## Research question

Propose one specific, testable hypothesis connecting phosphorylation of a nuclear-pore-complex nucleoporin to ALS-related neuronal dysfunction. Explain the causal chain, distinguish an initiating mechanism from a downstream response, and propose an experimental strategy that discriminates the hypothesis from an alternative. Identify supported premises, speculative bridges, and a falsifying observation. This adapts Co-Scientist Supplementary Note 10; nucleoporin phosphorylation is not supplied as an established ALS cause.

## S1 — TDP-43 and nuclear-pore dysfunction

Chou et al. (2018), *TDP-43 pathology disrupts nuclear pore complexes and nucleocytoplasmic transport in ALS/FTD*. Nature Neuroscience. DOI: `10.1038/s41593-017-0047-3`; PMID: `29311743`; PMCID: `PMC5800968`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29311743/).

Nuclear-pore and transport components were associated with insoluble TDP-43 aggregates. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupted nucleoporin localization and nuclear transport in experimental cell systems; relevant pore pathology was observed in ALS tissue. This supports examining the connection between TDP-43 pathology and transport disruption. It does not identify a nucleoporin phosphorylation event as the initiating cause or establish the same sequence in every ALS subtype.

## S2 — C9orf72-associated transport defects

Zhang et al. (2015), *The C9orf72 repeat expansion disrupts nucleocytoplasmic transport*. Nature. DOI: `10.1038/nature14973`; PMID: `26308891`; PMCID: `PMC4800742`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26308891/).

Expanded C9orf72 repeat RNA was linked to altered RanGAP localization and impaired nuclear import in models and patient-derived neurons. Manipulations of transport or repeat-RNA-associated mechanisms modified model phenotypes. This supplies a genetic-context-specific route to transport dysfunction. It does not show that sporadic ALS arises by the same route or directly establish a nucleoporin phosphorylation mechanism.

## S3 — A stress-granule-independent route

Gasset-Rosa et al. (2019), *Cytoplasmic TDP-43 De-mixing Independent of Stress Granules Drives Inhibition of Nuclear Import, Loss of Nuclear TDP-43, and Cell Death*. Neuron. DOI: `10.1016/j.neuron.2019.02.038`; PMID: `30853299`; PMCID: `PMC6548321`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30853299/).

Persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies could form independently of conventional stress granules. They recruited or mislocalized transport-associated proteins and were associated with impaired transport, nuclear TDP-43 depletion, and cell death. Phosphorylated TDP-43 accumulated in these assemblies. That is not itself evidence of nucleoporin phosphorylation. The experimental perturbations do not establish that every physiological ALS trajectory begins in this way.

## S4 — A stress-granule-associated route

Zhang et al. (2018), *Stress Granule Assembly Disrupts Nucleocytoplasmic Transport*. Cell. DOI: `10.1016/j.cell.2018.03.025`; PMID: `29628143`; PMCID: `PMC6083872`. [Primary record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29628143/).

Cellular stress recruited transport factors into stress granules and impaired nucleocytoplasmic transport. Altering stress-granule assembly modified transport defects and disease-model phenotypes. This provides a sequestration-based alternative to an intrinsic pore-modification hypothesis. Read alongside S3, it does not justify assuming that conventional stress granules are required for every TDP-43-associated transport defect.

## Evidence boundaries

- These selected passages do not establish that nucleoporin phosphorylation initiates ALS. Label a proposed kinase, modification site, or interaction as an assumption unless a supplied source supports it.
- Specify the ALS context; do not assume a universal mechanism across genetic and sporadic disease.
- Distinguish pore alteration, transport-factor sequestration, and failure secondary to broader stress.
- Explain temporal and perturbational evidence that would distinguish cause from consequence.
- Propose a research hypothesis rather than claiming a mechanism or treatment has been validated.


Proposed answer (the answer to evaluate):
p38α-Dependent NUP62 Phosphorylation as an Initiator of Nuclear-Import Failure in TARDBP-M337V Motor Neurons

Hypothesis. In TARDBP-p.M337V human motor neurons, p38α-dependent phosphorylation of pore-associated NUP62 reduces pore retention, initiating nuclear-import failure before persistent cytoplasmic TDP-43 assemblies appear. Impaired import then promotes nuclear TDP-43 depletion and neuronal dysfunction. This proposes an initiator of transport dysfunction in one ALS context, not the earliest cause of ALS or a universal mechanism.

Evidence and selection limits. Disease-linked TDP-43 disrupts nucleoporin localization and transport in models, with pore pathology also observed in ALS tissue [S1]. Persistent TDP-43 assemblies provide a stress-granule-independent transport-disruption route [S3]; conventional stress granules provide a sequestration alternative [S4]. C9orf72-associated RanGAP/import abnormalities supply a distinct genetic-context-specific route [S2]. None establishes initiating NUP62 phosphorylation; phosphorylated TDP-43 is not phosphorylated NUP62. Pair selection uses unverified prior knowledge that p38α is stress-responsive and NUP62 is an FG-channel nucleoporin. Its priority is experimentally separable kinase, phosphosite, and retention interventions—not established superiority over other combinations. Activity-matched JNK/NUP62 and p38α/NUP98 biochemical comparisons benchmark specificity rather than introduce additional disease hypotheses. Direct phosphorylation and retention-dependent dysfunction remain assumptions; novelty beyond the packet is unestablished.

Model and decision rules. Use two TARDBP-p.M337V patient-iPSC backgrounds, their isogenic corrections, independent clones, and blinded differentiations; allele selection is unverified prior knowledge. The primary endpoint is the fitted first-five-minute import-rate constant of a cytoplasm-photoactivated classical-NLS reporter, with size-matched NLS-deficient controls and experimentally verified importin-α/β dependence. Six-hourly measurements track import, p38α activity, pore-associated NUP62 phosphorylation, occupancy/residence time, TDP-43 distribution, both assembly types, energy status, electrophysiology, and survival. Operational onset is a ≥20% import-rate decrease at two successive samples; phosphorylation and retention loss must precede onset by ≥6 hours and precede energetic collapse. Prespecify sites with mass-spectrometry localization probability ≥0.95, ≥2-fold mutant enrichment, ≥50% reduction after p38α suppression, and direct phosphorylation by purified active—but not inactive—p38α. Freeze all qualifying sites before causal tests in independent cultures. Rescue requires ≥50% recovery of the mutant-control deficit, with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero. These are operational thresholds, not established biological boundaries.

Causality and retention mediation. Edit qualifying endogenous sites to phosphorylation-resistant residues, retaining wild-type revertants. Require normal baseline NUP62 abundance, import, scaffold organization/pore density, and passive dextran permeability. Complement editing with genetic p38α suppression and acute activation calibrated to measured mutant kinase activity: activation should impair import only when NUP62 remains phosphorylatable. For an independent retention rescue, use an inducible NUP62–NUP93 tether; anchor selection rests on unverified prior knowledge, and tether compatibility requires validation. Confirm unchanged NUP62 phosphorylation and no tether-induced integrity/permeability changes; include nonbinding-tether and ligand-only controls. Tether rescue despite continued phosphorylation and upstream stress would support retention as the mediator. Phosphosite rescue alone cannot establish that mediation because substitutions might alter other interactions.

Competing explanations and preparation controls. Transport-factor sequestration or broader stress could precede NUP62 phosphorylation [S3, S4]. Test G3BP1/2 CRISPRi against conventional granules—an unverified-prior-knowledge intervention choice—and a proposed cytoplasm-restricted TDP-43 degrader against persistent TDP-43 assemblies. Validate selective structure loss, preserved nuclear TDP-43, and unchanged basal transport; reagent nonselectivity makes the comparison uninterpretable. Earlier sequestration and assembly-only rescue without NUP62-site protection favor the alternative. Measure kinase activity and phosphorylation to exclude rescue merely through reduced upstream stress. In permeabilized neurons, cross control/mutant cytosol and perform defined import-factor add-back. Verify phosphosite occupancy, NUP62 localization, and pore integrity before and after preparation. A retained, phosphosite-dependent defect with identical soluble factors supports pore-intrinsic dysfunction. Normalization alone cannot prove sequestration: preparation may erase the lesion, or excess factors may compensate for it.

Falsification and limitations. In affected cultures, verified elimination of qualifying phosphorylation without baseline impairment, followed by unchanged early import failure and neuronal dysfunction with confidence intervals excluding ≥20% rescue, would falsify the proposed chain. Reproducible import failure preceding phosphorylation would contradict initiation even if phosphorylation later amplifies dysfunction. Limitations include immature neurons, matched-culture rather than single-cell phosphoproteomic timing, limited temporal resolution, phosphosite/tether structural effects, unvalidated degrader selectivity, and reporter-specific transport behavior. A positive result would establish a context-limited preclinical mechanism, not clinical efficacy or universality across ALS.

Ranked proposal:
p38α-Dependent NUP62 Phosphorylation as an Initiator of Nuclear-Import Failure in TARDBP-M337V Motor Neurons
